g1.label: 1. Not all of it is ___
g1.why: The text warns that not all internet information is reliable.

g2.label: 2. Anyone can write a ___
g2.why: The text says anyone can create a website or write a blog.

g3.label: 3. Edited by thousands of ___
g3.why: The text says a wiki like Wikipedia is written and edited by thousands of volunteers.

g4.label: 4. It can contain ___
g4.why: The text says wikis are up to date but can also contain mistakes.

g5.label: 5. Check the ___
g5.why: The text says you should check the sources listed at the bottom of an article.

g6.label: 6. Websites spread ___
g6.why: The text says some websites spread hoaxes — false stories designed to trick people.

g7.label: 7. A trusted ___
g7.why: The text says to check whether something comes from a trusted source.

g8.label: 8. Online ___
g8.why: The text says online reviews from other users can help you judge a product.

g1.label: 1. A website you can trust
g1.why: ‘Reliable’ means a website you can trust and believe.

g2.label: 2. Google and Bing
g2.why: Google and Bing are examples of a search engine.

g3.label: 3. A personal online diary
g3.why: A personal online diary where someone shares opinions is called a blog.

g4.label: 4. A false story to trick people
g4.why: A false story created to trick people is called a hoax.

g5.label: 5. Where information comes from
g5.why: The place information originally comes from is called the source.

g6.label: 6. A changed wiki gets an ___
g6.why: When a wiki is changed to add new information, it gets an update.

g7.label: 7. A customer comment
g7.why: A comment from a customer about a product is called a review.

g8.label: 8. Information that is not true
g8.why: Information that is not true or not real is called fake.
